lesson: Ensure all necessary dependencies are installed and correctly configured before running tests.
Verify that environment variables are properly set for all required configurations.
Implement comprehensive test coverage to catch potential issues early in the development cycle.
Ensure that all components and modules are correctly imported and used in the application.
Ensure that the import statements in React components match the actual exports in the imported modules.
Avoid using nested React Router components to prevent runtime errors and ensure proper routing.
Always declare and import dependencies in React components to prevent runtime ReferenceErrors.
A React component should not render its own <Routes> if the route table is already defined in a parent component to prevent duplicate rendering and navigation state issues.
Ensure that all destructured props in React components are correctly passed from their parent components.
React components should not redeclare routes that are already managed by a parent component to prevent double rendering and navigation state issues.
Ensure that imported modules match their export types; if a module exports named functions, import them accordingly to avoid runtime errors.
React components should properly utilize props passed from their parent components to maintain data flow and functionality.
React components should consistently import named exports from a module, avoiding default imports when the module only provides named exports.
Ensure that all React components handle potential errors during rendering to prevent the entire app from crashing.
When using React, verify that all imported components and modules are correctly configured and that their exports match the imports.
Ensure all named exports are correctly imported in React components.
Wrap the entire React app with a <BrowserRouter> or <RouterProvider> to enable routing.
Verify that components accept all necessary props passed by their callers.
Define all global variables and dependencies at the top level of your application to prevent runtime errors.
React components should import named exports correctly from their respective modules.
React components should utilize all props passed to them from their parent components.

Ensure that imported modules use the correct named exports. For example, if a module exports named functions like `load`, `save`, and `clearSettings`, the import statement should specify these names explicitly.
Avoid nested React Router components to prevent runtime errors. Ensure that only one instance of `BrowserRouter` or `HashRouter` is used in the application.
Verify that components accept all necessary props passed by their parents. Ensure that destructuring in component props includes all expected properties.
Handle potential null or undefined data before using array methods like `map` to prevent runtime errors. Ensure that data is properly initialized and validated before rendering.
